what: Code-reading card check of the 17 gauntlet cards not checked before (Sept 26, 2026), official engine 7fc6ccb (engine/src; git diff 7fc6ccb HEAD -- engine/src is empty). Three checkers (one per list), then three independent skeptics on every finding that was not clean, plus a spot-check of the verdicts most likely to change play. Pre-repair; re-check at the repaired engine.

row.subject: A2b 055 = Varoom (Metal Basic, 70 HP), 2 copies in g-mega_scizor_revavroom.txt
row.card_text: Varoom [A2b 055] Metal, Basic, HP 70, weak Fire, retreat 1. [M] Headbutt 10.

findings.clause: Identity: Metal, Basic, 70 HP, weak Fire, retreat 1, worth 1 point
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values. Not ex and not Mega, so 1 point. Weakness is a flat +20 from Fire attackers on the Active only.
findings.evidence: engine/src/database.rs 16746-16767; models/card.rs 186-216 (is_ex, is_mega, get_knockout_points); hooks/core.rs 1488-1512 (printed_weakness_application, Flat(20) at 1509), 1787-1793 (Weakness only when is_active_to_active). lib/card.py output matches.

findings.clause: [M] Headbutt 10, no effect
findings.engine_does: Plain 10 damage to the opponent's Active (effect None, so no mechanic lookup). Needs one [M], so the player going first cannot use it on turn 1. Training Area gives nothing (Basic).

findings.clause: Base of Revavroom B2b 050 (evolves from 'Varoom')
findings.engine_does: Evolution matches by name, so this printing (Headbutt) evolves into Revavroom B2b 050 like the B2b 049 printing. Normal gates: not on either player's first turn, not the turn it was played, once per turn.

row.subject: B2a 077 = Orthworm (Metal Basic, 100 HP), 1 copy
row.card_text: Orthworm [B2a 077] Metal, Basic, HP 100, weak Fire, retreat 3. [M] Iron Supply 10 — "Take a [M] Energy from your Energy Zone and attach it to 1 of your Benched Pokémon."

findings.clause: Identity: Metal, Basic, 100 HP, weak Fire, retreat 3, worth 1 point
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values.

findings.clause: Iron Supply: [M], 10 damage
findings.engine_does: Maps the exact text to ChargeBench{energies:[Metal], target_benched_type:None}; the 10 damage is dealt to the opponent's Active through active_damage_effect_doutcome, then the attach effect runs.
findings.evidence: actions/effect_mechanic_map.rs 2900-2906; apply_attack_action.rs 422-425, 2318-2345; actions/mutations.rs 22-27. No engine test names Iron Supply.

findings.clause: Take a [M] Energy from your Energy Zone and attach it to 1 of your Benched Pokémon (who chooses, which targets)
findings.engine_does: Pushes one Attach choice per Benched Pokémon of the attacker (any type or stage, never the Active); the attacking player picks. It creates a Metal Energy with is_turn_energy=false, so the turn's Energy Zone attachment is untouched and the Energy is Metal whatever the zone shows. Mandatory once the attack resolves (no Noop), as the text reads.
findings.evidence: apply_attack_action.rs 2324-2344; apply_action.rs 783-786, 949-964; state/energy.rs 13-33 (energy_zone.current cleared only when is_turn_energy).

findings.clause: Empty Bench: does the attack still work and do 10?
findings.engine_does: Yes. With no Benched Pokémon the choice list is empty and the effect returns, but the 10 damage is already part of the outcome. (The comment at 2339 says 'no damage applied'; it is stale, the damage is dealt.) Offered normally with an empty Bench, which fits the card: the attack does something (10 damage).

findings.clause: Order with knockouts and retaliation
findings.engine_does: Damage, then the attach choice, then Rocky Helmet-style retaliation, then knockouts and promotion. Matches the rules order (attack effects before retaliation and Knock Outs).

row.subject: B2b 001 = Scyther (Grass Basic, 70 HP), 2 copies
row.card_text: Scyther [B2b 001] Grass, Basic, HP 70, weak Fire, retreat 1. [C] U-turn 10 — "Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon."

findings.clause: Identity: Grass, Basic, 70 HP, weak Fire, retreat 1, worth 1 point
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values. Being Grass, it is not a legal target for Metal Transport's 'Active [M] Pokémon' and gets nothing from Metal Core Barrier until it Mega Evolves (the Tool is kept on evolution).

findings.clause: U-turn: [C], 10 damage, then switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon (mandatory, player chooses)
findings.engine_does: Maps to SwitchSelfWithBench (optional=false, so no Noop). Deals 10, then pushes one Activate choice per Benched Pokémon for the attacker. The switch runs through apply_activate: Scyther's Special Conditions and attack effects are cleared, and it is not a retreat (has_retreated untouched).

findings.clause: U-turn with an empty Bench
findings.engine_does: Still does 10; no switch frame is pushed.

findings.clause: U-turn into Rocky Helmet (Blaziken panel deck)
findings.engine_does: The switch resolves before retaliation, and apply_activate remaps the pending retaliation frame, so the 20 lands on Scyther on the Bench. That is the rules order (the attack's effects, then retaliation). The Pokémon switched in gets the 'moved' flag, but the attack ends the turn and the flag is reset before its next turn.
findings.evidence: attack_outcome.rs 161-202; apply_action_helpers.rs 942-956; state/mod.rs 1205. Test: actions/bench_switch_target_tests.rs 185-235 (Yanma's U-turn, same text, with a double KO).

findings.clause: Evolves into Mega Scizor ex
findings.engine_does: By name 'Scyther', with the normal gates (not first turn, not the turn played, once per turn).

row.subject: B2b 047 = Mega Scizor ex (Metal Stage 1 from Scyther, 200 HP, Mega ex), 2 copies
row.card_text: Mega Scizor ex [B2b 047] Metal, Stage 1 (from Scyther), HP 200, weak Fire, retreat 2. [MMC] Bullet Slugger 100 — "If this Pokémon moved from your Bench to the Active Spot this turn, this attack does 50 more damage." Mega Evolution ex: 3 points when Knocked Out; Mega Evolving does not end the turn.

findings.clause: Identity: Metal, Stage 1 from 'Scyther', 200 HP, weak Fire, retreat 2, Mega ex worth 3 points
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values; the 'Mega ' prefix gives 3 points and the last word 'ex' makes it an ex for Red and similar effects.

findings.clause: Mega Evolving does not end the turn; evolution keeps damage, Energy and Tools and clears conditions and attack effects
findings.engine_does: apply_evolve builds a fresh PlayedCard carrying damage, Energy, Tools and the cards behind; nothing ends the turn (only an Attack sets end_turn_pending).

findings.clause: Bullet Slugger: [MMC] 100, +50 if this Pokémon moved from your Bench to the Active Spot this turn
findings.engine_does: Maps to ExtraDamageIfMovedFromBench{50}; reads moved_to_active_this_turn on the attacker's Active and passes 100 or 150 as the attack's base damage into modify_damage, where Training Area (+10, Stage 1) and Red (+20 vs an Active ex) are added before Weakness, then defender reductions.

findings.clause: Which moves set the flag: own retreat, Metal Transport, switch cards (all during your turn)
findings.engine_does: The only place the flag is set is apply_activate, reached by paid Retreat, by Activate (Metal Transport, U-turn, Sabrina/Cyrus/Lyra-style switches) and by Promote. Own retreat and Metal Transport give +50, as the official Scizor ruling says for your own retreat or switch during your turn.
findings.evidence: apply_action_helpers.rs 963-965 (only setter); apply_action.rs 823-831, 1431-1468. Tests: tests/mega_scizor_ex_test.rs 29-51 (no move: 100), 53-91 (retreat: 150), 93-135 (Metal Transport from a Benched Revavroom: 150), 137-190 (Lyra: 150). Ruling: rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md 33; rules/_research_notes/detailed_battle_faq.md 76-77.

findings.clause: Flag reset each turn
findings.engine_does: advance_turn calls end_turn_maintenance for every Pokémon of both players, which clears moved_to_active_this_turn (also cleared at game start). So a move on the opponent's turn never carries into yours, provided it happens before advance_turn.

findings.clause: Opponent's switches on their turn (Sabrina: Altaria, Hydreigon, Sceptile, Vespiquen decks; Cyrus: most panel decks) and promotion after the opponent's ATTACK knocks out your Active
findings.engine_does: No +50 on your turn: the switch or the Promote frame resolves on the opponent's turn (the stack has priority over EndTurn), and advance_turn then clears the flag. Matches the official ruling (a Pokémon promoted after a Knock Out on the opponent's turn does not count).

findings.clause: Promotion after a Knock Out at the END of the opponent's turn or at the Pokémon Checkup after it (Burn, Poison, Deceptive Needle, Bad Dreams)
findings.engine_does: Gives the +50. The end-of-turn effects, the Checkup and advance_turn run in one mutation; the knockout's Promote frame is inserted at the bottom of the stack and resolves only after advance_turn has cleared the flags (and after the next player's draw). apply_activate then sets moved_to_active_this_turn during YOUR turn, and it survives to your attack: a promoted Mega Scizor ex with [MMC] hits 150 instead of 100 (160 with Training Area, 180 with Red vs an ex). The official ruling says the bonus applies only to a move during your turn and not after a promotion following a Knock Out on the opponent's turn. Dustin's footage shows Pocket asks for the new Active before the next turn starts (Altaria check, deviation 3). Pocket's behaviour for this exact Scizor case has not been observed, but the text, the ruling and the footage all say no bonus. rules/05 #20 and rules/07 line 185 say the engine gets opponent-turn promotion right; they covered only the attack-KO case. Reachable against 5 of the 8 panel decks: Blaziken (Mega Burning Burn; Castform Sunny Scorching Burn whenever any Stadium, including this list's own Training Area, is in play), Weezing (Boiler Smog Poison+Burn; Deceptive Needle 10 at the end of their turn), Hydreigon (Deceptive Needle), Altaria (Bad Dreams 20 at the end of their turn on an Asleep Active), Sceptile (Terminating Tail Poison). It changes damage thresholds, for example 160 vs 110 into a 150-HP Hydreigon with Training Area. Repair note: fixing the known promotion-timing deviation only fixes this if the promotion resolves before end_turn_maintenance, or if Promote no longer sets the flag.
findings.evidence: apply_action_helpers.rs 109-116 (on_end_turn then the Checkup phase), 146-166, 326 (handle_knockouts inside the Checkup), 337-339 (advance_turn); state/mod.rs 1391-1423 (Promote frame inserted at the stack bottom), 1205-1206 (flag reset, then draw queued); apply_action.rs 827-830 -> apply_action_helpers.rs 963-965 (Promote sets the flag); apply_attack_action.rs 4914-4919 (read at attack). End-of-turn damage: hooks/core.rs 580-603 (Deceptive Needle), 618-654 (Bad Dreams), both via handle_damage -> handle_knockouts (apply_action_helpers.rs 495-514). Footage: rl/results/altaria_card_check_2026-09-26/README.md 33-43. Ruling: rules/_research_notes/detailed_battle_faq.md 76-77. No engine test covers this path.

findings.clause: Scyther moved to the Active Spot, then Mega Evolved the same turn
findings.engine_does: No +50: apply_evolve replaces the PlayedCard with a fresh one (moved_to_active_this_turn=false). This matches the official Scizor ruling ('NOT when Scyther moved up and then evolved into Scizor that turn'), so it is not open. Evolving on the Bench first and then switching in gives +50 in both.

findings.clause: Promotion after your own Active is Knocked Out during your own turn (rules/05 #20)
findings.engine_does: Would count it as moved (Promote sets the flag during your turn). Open in Pocket. Unreachable in gauntlet games: nothing in this list damages its own Pokémon, the panel decks' damaging Abilities and Tools fire on their own turn or at the end of a turn, and Rocky Helmet fires only after your attack.

row.subject: B2b 050 = Revavroom (Metal Stage 1 from Varoom, 110 HP, Ability Metal Transport), 2 copies
row.card_text: Revavroom [B2b 050] Metal, Stage 1 (from Varoom), HP 110, weak Fire, retreat 3. Ability Metal Transport: "Once during your turn, you may switch your Active [M] Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon." [MC] Outta-Control Dash 60.

findings.clause: Identity: Metal, Stage 1 from 'Varoom', 110 HP, weak Fire, retreat 3, 1 point, one Tool slot
findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values. The two-Tool Dual Customization belongs to B4 115 only; this printing keeps one slot.

findings.clause: [MC] Outta-Control Dash 60, no effect
findings.engine_does: Plain 60; Training Area adds 10 (Stage 1) against the opponent's Active.

findings.clause: Metal Transport: only if your Active is a [M] Pokémon, and only with a Benched Pokémon to switch to
findings.engine_does: Maps the exact text to SwitchActiveTypedWithBench{Metal}. Offered only when the current Active counts as Metal and the Bench is not empty. So an Active Scyther (Grass) can't be switched out this way; an Active Varoom, Orthworm, Revavroom or Mega Scizor ex can.

findings.clause: Once during your turn, per Revavroom; from the Active or the Bench
findings.engine_does: ability_used is set on the Revavroom that used it, checked before offering it, and reset every turn. Two Revavroom give two uses. Every in-play Pokémon of the current player is scanned, so an Active or Benched Revavroom can use it. An Active Revavroom that uses it switches itself to the Bench and stays marked as used. A Revavroom that evolved this turn can use it at once, which is right for Abilities.
findings.evidence: apply_action_helpers.rs 997-1002, 957; move_generation_abilities.rs 13-23, 321-323; state/played_card.rs 474; test mega_scizor_ex_test.rs 93-135 (Benched Revavroom).

findings.clause: Who chooses the Benched Pokémon; 'you may'
findings.engine_does: Using the Ability is optional (it is an offered action). Once used, the owner picks any Benched Pokémon of any type; there is no cancel.

findings.clause: Switching removes Special Conditions and attack effects; it is not a retreat and works while Asleep or Paralyzed
findings.engine_does: The swap goes through apply_retreat(free) -> apply_activate, which clears conditions and effects on the Pokémon going to the Bench and does not set has_retreated or pay Energy. No status check gates the Ability. This cures Boiler Smog Poison+Burn (Weezing), Blaziken's Burn, Altaria's Sleep, and clears Bonsly's Teary Attack −30 (Lucario deck) from the Pokémon sent to the Bench.
findings.evidence: apply_action.rs 823-830, 1431-1435 (has_retreated only in the paid path, 1465); apply_action_helpers.rs 959-961; state/played_card.rs 378-386; rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md 30; RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md 102.

findings.clause: Does the Pokémon switched in count as 'moved from your Bench to the Active Spot this turn'?
findings.engine_does: Yes: apply_activate sets moved_to_active_this_turn on the incoming Pokémon, so a Benched Mega Scizor ex brought in by Metal Transport gets Bullet Slugger's +50 that turn. This matches the ruling (your own switch during your turn).

row.subject: A2b 071 = Red (Supporter), 1 copy
row.card_text: Red [A2b 071] Trainer (Supporter): "During this turn, attacks used by your Pokémon do +20 damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon ex."

findings.clause: Supporter: one per turn; playable on the first turn
findings.engine_does: Offered through the shared Supporter gate (one per turn, blocked by No-Supporter effects); no first-turn block.

findings.clause: During this turn
findings.engine_does: Adds TurnEffect::IncreasedDamageAgainstEx{20} for the current turn number only (duration 0). It is player-wide, not tied to a Pokémon, so it still applies after switching or Metal Transport that turn.

findings.clause: +20 only by attacks, only to the opponent's ACTIVE Pokémon ex
findings.engine_does: Counted only when is_active_to_active (target slot 0, attacker slot 0, attack damage) and the target is an ex (Mega ex included). Benched targets, non-ex targets, Poison/Burn and Ability damage get nothing.
findings.evidence: hooks/core.rs 1059-1063, 1737-1738, 1767-1774; models/card.rs 186-194. Test: hooks/core.rs 2618-2672 (no bonus vs non-ex, +20 vs ex).

findings.clause: Stacking and order relative to Weakness
findings.engine_does: Summed with the other attacker-side boosts (Training Area +10 and the attack's own bonus, such as Bullet Slugger's 150) before Weakness, then defender reductions (such as Shuckle ex's Solid Shell −20 in the Vespiquen deck) after. Example: Bullet Slugger 150 + 20 + 10 = 180, +20 into an ex weak to Metal.

findings.clause: Side of the target (code note)
findings.engine_does: is_active_to_active does not check that the target is the opponent's. Unreachable: self-damage recoil is applied directly, not through modify_damage, and nothing in this list attacks its own Active.

findings.clause: Playable when it visibly can't work (the opponent's Active is not an ex and nothing this turn can change that)
findings.engine_does: Always offered (can_play_trainer). Whether Pocket blocks Red in that case (Dustin's playability rule) is unverified. Playing it only wastes the player's own Supporter, and nothing in this list rewards 'a Supporter played this turn', so no play change.

row.subject: B2 148 = Metal Core Barrier (Pokémon Tool), 2 copies
row.card_text: Metal Core Barrier [B2 148] Trainer (Pokémon Tool): "If this card is attached to 1 of your Pokémon, discard it at the end of your opponent's turn.The [M] Pokémon this card is attached to takes -50 damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon."

findings.clause: Attachable to any of your Pokémon (one Tool each); effect matched by text
findings.engine_does: Tools can go on any Pokémon with a free slot; effects are gated where they apply. Tools are matched by effect text, so both printings (B2 148, B2b 117) count. (The database text has no space after 'turn.', which is cosmetic and matches card.py.)

findings.clause: −50 only on a [M] holder; non-Metal holder gets nothing
findings.engine_does: Reduction is 50 × copies only if the holder counts as Metal. A Scyther holding it gets nothing; once it Mega Evolves the Tool carries over and works.

findings.clause: Only damage from attacks (not Ability damage, not Poison/Burn, not Rocky Helmet-style damage)
findings.engine_does: Returns 0 unless is_from_active_attack. The Checkup passes false for Poison and Burn. Rocky Helmet retaliation is applied straight to the attacker without modify_damage. Deceptive Needle (Weezing, Hydreigon), Bad Dreams (Altaria) and Nightmare Aura (Weezing's Darkrai ex) all pass false. So none of them is reduced, which matches the official Mimikyu ex FAQ rule.

findings.clause: Also on the Bench (the text has no Active-only limit)
findings.engine_does: No slot check, so Bench snipes from attacks are reduced too: Heatmor Tongue Whip 30 and Hitmonlee Stretch Kick 30 become 0, Grovyle Slicing Snipe 50 becomes 0, Hoopa ex's Bench 20 becomes 0, and Chien-Pao ex's Diving Icicles 130 becomes 80.
findings.evidence: hooks/core.rs 715-735 (no target_idx test); attack_outcome.rs 146-155 (attack damage passes true for every target).

findings.clause: Order: attack damage -> attacker boosts -> Weakness -> defender reductions, never below 0
findings.engine_does: Weakness is added to the boosted pre-Weakness sum, and then Metal Core Barrier and the other reductions are subtracted with saturation. Every Pokémon in this list is weak to Fire: Mega Blaziken ex's Mega Burning 120 +20 −50 = 90 on Mega Scizor ex. Fighting Coach and Arena of Antiquity (Lucario deck) add before Weakness, and the Barrier comes off after.
findings.evidence: hooks/core.rs 1854-1885, 1309-1341. Test: tests/rules_repair_damage_opening.rs 172-202 (60 Fire under Bounded Field into Skarmory ex with the Barrier = 70, as in Dustin's game; 10 -> 0; 0 -> 0).

findings.clause: Discarded at the end of your opponent's turn (not your own)
findings.engine_does: At the end of each player's turn, on_end_turn discards every Metal Core Barrier from the OTHER player's Pokémon. So one attached on your turn survives your turn's end, protects through the opponent's turn and is discarded at its end, whatever the holder's type. This happens before that Checkup, which does not matter since the Barrier never reduces Checkup damage.
findings.evidence: hooks/core.rs 381, 504-519. Test: tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs 663-681. Seen in play: rules/_research_notes/R1_battle_observations.md 145.

findings.clause: 'from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon': attacks by your own side
findings.engine_does: The Barrier does not check the attacker's side, unlike Heavy Helmet and Steel Apron. An attack that damages its user's own [M] Pokémon holding the Barrier through the damage-target list would be wrongly reduced. Unreachable here: no card in this list attacks its own side, recoil such as Hoopa ex's Dynamite Punch is applied directly without modify_damage, and no panel deck runs the Barrier.
findings.evidence: hooks/core.rs 715-735 compared with 693 (Heavy Helmet) and 743 (Steel Apron); apply_attack_action.rs 3143-3148.

findings.engine_does: Stores exactly these values.

findings.engine_does: Needs at least one Fire, at least one Lightning and a third Energy of either type. F,F,F or L,L,L cannot attack; F,L alone cannot either.

findings.clause: 100 damage to the opponent's Active
findings.engine_does: Plain 100 through modify_damage: attacker boosts, then Weakness (none possible here), then defender reductions (Shuckle ex Solid Shell -20, Frigibax P-B 037 Stiffen -20), floored at 0.

findings.clause: -30 to damage from attacks during the opponent's next turn only
findings.engine_does: When the discard choice resolves, it adds CardEffect::ReducedDamage{30} with duration 1 to the attacker. end_turn_maintenance runs on all Pokémon of both players at each turn change: 1 becomes 0 at the end of our turn, and the effect is dropped at the end of the opponent's turn. The reduction is read only for active-to-active attack damage (is_from_active_attack), after Weakness, stacking with other reductions and floored at 0. So it ignores Poison/Burn ticks, Bad Dreams (Darkrai B2b 040), Nightmare Aura (Darkrai ex) and Deceptive Needle (passed is_from_active_attack=false). Opponent attacks that pick our Active as a target (Chien-Pao ex Diving Icicles) still count as active-to-active.

1.reasoning: Every step holds. The flag is PlayedCard.moved_to_active_this_turn. It starts false, and its only setter is apply_activate, which is reached by paid Retreat, by Activate (Metal Transport, U-turn, switch Supporters) and by Promote (apply_action.rs 823-830 -> apply_retreat(is_free=true) -> apply_activate). It is cleared only by PlayedCard::end_turn_maintenance, which State::end_turn_maintenance runs for both players from advance_turn. Bullet Slugger reads it at attack time. Path for an end-of-turn knockout: the EndTurn mutation runs on_end_turn (Bad Dreams, Deceptive Needle -> handle_damage -> handle_knockouts -> trigger_promotion_or_declare_winner). That inserts the Promote frame at index 0, or at the phase floor. The same mutation then runs the Checkup, whose knockouts also insert Promote at the bottom, then advance_turn. advance_turn switches current_player, increments turn_count, runs end_turn_maintenance and PUSHES DrawCard on top. The stack top is last(), so the new turn's draw resolves first and Promote after it. Both happen inside the new turn, and nothing clears the flag again before the attack. So a Benched Mega Scizor ex promoted after a Burn, Poison, Needle or Bad Dreams knockout on the opponent's turn gets +50. A knockout from the opponent's ATTACK is handled right: the stack frame outranks the end_turn_pending EndTurn, so the promotion resolves on the opponent's turn and advance_turn clears the flag. The official ruling is for Scizor A4 123's Gale Thrust, whose condition text is word for word Bullet Slugger's (both checked with card.py). It excludes promotion after a Knock Out on the opponent's turn, and the footage (deviation 3) shows Pocket promotes before the next turn starts. Reachability: Mega Scizor ex is a Stage 1 from Scyther, so it can sit on the Bench (Scyther benched, then evolved there). Benching it is this list's natural Metal Transport line, and the list runs 2. Five panel decks deal end-of-turn or Checkup damage. Blaziken: Mega Burning Burn, plus Castform's Sunny Scorching with any Stadium in play, and t-blaziken runs its own Hiking Trail as well as the Scizor list's Training Area. Weezing: Boiler Smog Poison+Burn, Deceptive Needle. Hydreigon: Deceptive Needle. Altaria: Darkrai's Bad Dreams. Sceptile: Terminating Tail Poison. Lucario, Suicune and Vespiquen deal none. Two limits on how much it matters. First, when a Revavroom with Metal Transport unused and another Metal Pokémon on the Bench are available, the player could get +50 legally by promoting that Pokémon and transporting Scizor in. The deviation gives it free, saves the Transport, and works with no Revavroom at all. Second, the coverage file says the pilot's estimator prices Bullet Slugger at printed damage, so the bot may not choose the promotion for the bonus, but the engine still deals 150. Damage thresholds change (for example 160 vs 110 into a 150 HP Hydreigon with Training Area). Frequency is unknown without game logs (none at action level exist; smoke runs record only outcomes). The repair note is right: fixing deviation 3 fixes this only if Promote resolves before advance_turn's end_turn_maintenance.

A KO at the Checkup after the Scizor player's OWN turn is promoted during the opponent's turn and cleared: also no bonus.
